note: Newest first. One entry per thing a player would notice. Dates are the day it went live.

entries.title: The narrator narrates again
entries.body: Briefings were reciting dice — "rolling a 4, drift neutral" — and flattening big ideas into menu orders. Now the arithmetic stays on the board and the prose tells you what it meant. Say you are a pacifist society that sells flattering sketches and the world remembers it, prices it as its own scheme, and the neighbours form opinions. The end-of-world chronicle opens on what happened while you were not looking.

entries.title: Playable in a browser
entries.body: The world you could only run inside Claude Code now runs at unstuck-games.com/elsewhere/play — password-gated while it is early. Python still rolls the dice; three small models do the talking.

entries.title: A home of our own
entries.body: Every game moved to unstuck-games.com, off a borrowed address and onto a machine we run. Any game now opens the studio picker, so you are never stranded on a page with no way back to the rest.

entries.title: God Mode: one ad a day, hours on tap
entries.body: One ad per game per day. After that, switch God Mode on for an hour whenever you like until tomorrow, free. No second ad, no chain, no energy, no currency. Surely you have to watch another one? No. Go play.

entries.title: Lucy has a page, and a newsletter
entries.body: A launcher game about a long animal, except you do not aim her. One email when the door opens.
